How to start a reference article on EDFM.

== Choose one clear subject ==
A reference article explains what its subject is, the facts and mechanics directly associated with it, and the limitations a commander needs to understand. It includes enough adjacent context to answer the obvious questions, then links to the page that owns each related subject.

Do not turn a reference page into a complete activity guide. A commodity page may identify the mining methods that produce the commodity, but the ordered mining workflow belongs in a Field Procedure. A module page may explain what the module does and the information it returns, but a full activity loop belongs in the relevant guide.

See [[Elite Dangerous Field Manual:Editorial Policy#Topic ownership and page scope|Topic ownership and page scope]] for the site-wide rule.

== Before you start ==
Search for the subject and its common alternative names. Check whether the information belongs on an existing page or within an established topic hub from [[Main Page]].

Create a separate article when the subject has enough identity, facts, mechanics, or relationships to support one. Minor details that fit naturally within an existing article do not need their own pages.

If the page's subject is an ordered task rather than a reference topic, use [[Elite Dangerous Field Manual:Creating a Guide]] instead.

== Reference-page boundaries ==
Common reference types follow these boundaries:

* '''Ships and vehicles''' cover identity, manufacturer, acquisition, stock configuration, internal slots, hardpoints, utility mounts, built-in equipment, capacity, performance, inherent capabilities, and limitations. Builds, activity tactics, outfitting tutorials, and Engineering strategy remain separate.
* '''Modules''' cover specifications, classes, ratings, compatibility, direct mechanics, behaviour, and limitations. Procedures explain how to use the module during a larger activity.
* '''Engineers''' cover identity, location, discovery and meeting requirements, unlock requirement, services, maximum grades, version requirements, and direct referrals. Full unlock routes and Engineering strategy belong elsewhere.
* '''Commodities and materials''' cover classification, description, source environments, acquisition methods capable of producing them, uses, and subject-specific distribution or market information. Generic activity procedures remain separate.
* '''Locations and regions''' cover geography, significance, characteristics, and notable local services. Travel and activity guides are linked as their own subjects.

Useful information found on the wrong page must not be discarded. Confirm that the owning article represents it appropriately before removing substantial duplication.

== Title ==
Use a plain, flat, human-readable Main-namespace title, such as <code>[[Broo Tarquin]]</code>, not <code>Engineer:Broo Tarquin</code>. EDFM does not use artificial subject namespaces or slash-based article paths.

Create redirects for well-established abbreviations and alternative names according to [[Elite Dangerous Field Manual:Redirect and Disambiguation Policy]].

== Starting from a skeleton ==
Several subject types have subst-only skeleton templates. Check [[:Category:Templates]] for one matching the article, such as {{tl|New engineer page}}, {{tl|New blueprint page}}, {{tl|New engineering module page}}, or {{tl|New experimental effect page}}.

Enter <code><nowiki>{{subst:Template name}}</nowiki></code> as the first edit, using the actual template name. Substitution creates ordinary wikitext that can be edited independently.

Treat the result as a draft. Replace drafting prompts with finished content and remove sections that do not apply before the page is ready for readers. When no suitable skeleton exists, use {{tl|Article header}}, {{tl|Article status}}, and an appropriate infobox. See [[Elite Dangerous Field Manual:Adding Structured Data]] when the subject's data needs to be reused elsewhere.

== Verification and uncertainty ==
Do not invent values, compatibility, availability, requirements, locations, or mechanics. Check material claims against the live game or a reliable current source.

When a fact is genuinely uncertain or based on community testing, describe that uncertainty naturally and use the site's verification templates where appropriate. Do not publish drafting instructions, research tasks, or maintenance commentary as article prose.

== Links and categories ==
Link the article naturally to its topic hub, directly related reference subjects, and any procedure that teaches commanders how to use or obtain the subject. Avoid a large See also list that merely repeats links without context.

Every article needs at least one appropriate subject category. Gameplay-facing articles also use {{tl|Article status}}, which categorizes the page by review state and game mode. Browse <code>Special:Categories</code> or start from [[:Category:Gameplay]] before creating a new category.

== Before publication ==
Confirm that:

* the title and subject are unambiguous;
* every section directly explains the subject or supplies necessary context;
* detailed adjacent topics link to their owning pages;
* useful facts, citations, templates, categories, and structured data were preserved;
* uncertain claims are qualified and supported appropriately;
* links reach the intended pages and sections; and
* no visible drafting or implementation commentary remains.
